pick.counterargument: Growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +47.9%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $20.38 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-29, 7 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-05.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-24) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
stories.excerpt: Meta won't force Facebook page owners to allow AI training on linked content.
stories.lead:
“Does Meta think we can’t read?” Bamber wrote. He argued that removing the word “train” from the terms of service did little to reassure publishers, since “develop” posed the same threat.

“It’s saying it can use all the content it scrapes to develop ‘any business product’. I mean, come on,” he wrote.

Nieman Lab noted there was bipartisan concern in the US. Sens. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) sent letters asking Mark Zuckerberg to withdraw the terms.

stories.title: Introduction to Python SQL Libraries

stories.lead: All software applications interact with data, most commonly through a database management system (DBMS). Some programming languages come with modules that you can use to interact with a DBMS, while others require the use of third-party packages. In this tutorial, you’ll explore the different Python SQL libraries that you can use. You’ll develop a straightforward application to interact with SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL databases.

stories.title: All the latest updates on AI data centers
stories.excerpt: Massive new data centers are the physical foundation for tech companies’ hopes and dreams for AI. But the rush to expand warehouses full of energy-hungry servers has also kicked up fights across the world over their impact on power grids, utility bills, nearby communities, and the environment. Data…
stories.lead:
A massive permitting bill that could help energy projects come online much quicker and potentially lower utility bills for Americans is advancing with bipartisan support. And while it could be a catalyst for lots of clean energy, it could also speed up polluting projects and limit oversight of new data centers.

With data centers demanding more electricity for AI, environmental advocates fear that developers could take advantage of the reforms to evade public scrutiny and rely more heavily on fossil fuels. The bill sacrifices caution for speed, limiting environmental reviews and preventing communities from stopping a project from moving forward by taking it to court.

stories.excerpt: Thousands across the U.S. have gotten involved to oppose data centers. One is a Maryland woman who'd been evicted after a pay cut and became a leader of a community effort that blocked a vast project.
stories.lead:
The overgrown grass and weeds seem to stretch into the horizon on nearly 90 acres of empty land in Landover, Md. It used to be Landover Mall, but that closed in 2002, and the site has been mostly vacant since.

In 2024, the developer that built the mall won approval from county planners for a $5 billion data center campus, and word began spreading through the largely Black community nearby.

stories.title: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
stories.excerpt: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.
stories.lead:
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

stories.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
stories.excerpt: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
stories.lead:
Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.

The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.

The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

stories.title: This was the week the AI trade cracked. So what's next?

stories.lead: It has been a bumpy ride for AI and tech stocks this week. AI shares bounced back today. That was after suffering a huge loss yesterday that wiped out more than $2 trillion in value. Big Democratic victories have raised big fears about the outlook for AI, which, of course, is a game-changing technology, and tech companies are pouring a ton of money into developing it. It's not clear, though, if we are in the middle of a tech bubble that is about to burst.

stories.title: Water Polo Falls to #1 Cal in Overtime
stories.excerpt: Water falls to #1 Cal in overtime, 20-19.
stories.lead:
Berkeley, Calif. – It was the kind of game one would expect from two nationally-ranked teams when fifth-ranked Fordham traveled to face top-ranked California on Friday night. The visiting Rams gave the Golden Bears all they could handle, scoring three times in the final two minutes of regulation - including the tying goal at the buzzer - to force overtime where Cal outscored Fordham by a goal for a 20-19 win at the Avery Aquatic Center.

The loss snaps a 14-game winning streak for Fordham as the Rams fall to 23-2 on the season while Cal improves to 15-4.

stories.title: Croatia to get National Aquatics Centre in Zagreb
stories.excerpt: The Croatian government on 5 November 2026 approved a National Aquatics Centre in Zagreb, on the Faculty of Kinesiology site, with two Olympic pools, a diving pool and stands for 5,000. The post Croatia to get National Aquatics Centre in Zagreb appeared first on Total Waterpolo .
stories.lead:
Croatia is to get a National Aquatics Centre in Zagreb. The Croatian government approved the project at its session on Thursday, 5 November 2026.

Prime Minister Andrej Plenković announced the decision during the session. The centre, Nacionalni centar za vodene sportove, will be built on the site of today’s Faculty of Kinesiology. Plans include two Olympic pools, a diving pool and stands for 5,000 spectators.

According to the government and the Croatian Water Polo Federation (HVS), the decision was taken on the government’s initiative and in agreement with HVS and the Croatian Swimming Federation.
